content: Tigecycline is an antibiotic used to treat certain serious bacterial infections, particularly when other antibiotics are ineffective. It belongs to the tetracycline class of antibiotics and is not effective against viral infections such as the common cold or flu. This medication is administered intravenously over 30 to 60 minutes by a healthcare professional, typically every 12 hours as directed by your doctor. If you are using this medication at home, ensure you are properly trained in its preparation and administration. The solution should be gently swirled to mix, not shaken, and should appear yellow to orange in color. Do not use the medication if it contains particles or appears green or black. It is crucial to use this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals and to complete the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Stopping the medication prematurely may allow the infection to return or worsen. Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, and pain or swelling at the injection site. While these effects are generally mild, notify your doctor if they persist or worsen. Rarely, tigecycline and other tetracycline antibiotics can cause increased pressure around the brain (intracranial hypertension), which may lead to permanent vision loss or blindness. Women of childbearing age who are overweight or have a history of intracranial hypertension are at higher risk for this condition. Tigecycline may also rarely cause a severe intestinal condition due to Clostridium difficile bacteria, which can occur during or even weeks to months after treatment. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new yeast infection. This medication may increase sensitivity to sunlight. Limit sun exposure, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. Children under 8 years old are more susceptible to side effects, particularly tooth discoloration, which has also been observed in older children and young adults. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Tigecycline may harm an unborn baby, and it is unknown if it passes into breast milk. Avoid becoming pregnant while using this medication. Drug interactions can alter how tigecycline works or increase the risk of serious side effects. Provide your doctor and pharmacist with a complete list of all medications and supplements you are taking, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products. If an overdose occurs and serious symptoms such as fainting or difficulty breathing are present, call emergency services immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. In the U.S., you can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it for other infections unless directed by your doctor. Regular lab tests, such as liver function, fibrinogen levels, blood counts, and cultures, may be required to monitor your response to the medication. Keep all medical and lab appointments. Store this medication as directed by your pharmacist or the product instructions. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about tigecycline. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information tailored to your specific health needs.
